The '''EU LCS 2018 Spring Split''' was the first split of the 2018 [[European League of Legends Championship Series]] season, organized by Riot Games and held from January 19 to April 8, 2018. The season featured ten teams — eight returning from the [[LCS/Europe/2017/Summer|2017 Summer Split]] and two promoted from the [[LCS/Europe/2018/Spring/Promotion|2018 Spring Promotion]], [[FC Schalke 04 Esports]] and [[Giants Gaming]]. The split used a double round-robin format in the Group Stage with Best-of-One matches, followed by a Single Elimination Best-of-Five Playoffs to determine the European champion and the region’s representatives at the [[Mid-Season Invitational/2018|2018 Mid-Season Invitational]] while the top three teams would represent Europe at [[Rift_Rivals/2018/NA-EU|Rift Rivals 2018 – NA vs EU]].

This split was notable for being the last EU LCS season with a spring promotion tournament, as Riot Games announced that the league would transition to a [[LEC]] franchised system in 2019, eliminating relegation and promotion. As a result, there was no Summer Promotion Tournament for the 2018 season.
